_doc: Machine-readable index of open, batch-addressable backlog items for the Routine's systemic-fix mode (prompts/routine2.md §B). The wiki-maintenance session keeps this in sync with the prose backlog pages (ideas/cleanup-backlog.md, ideas/tooling-backlog.md). The selector (pipeline/routine_next.py) picks the lowest-'priority'-number item with status=='open' AND batch_ready==true. EVERY fix is verified per-entry before changing anything (the detectors are read-only review queues); 'fix_type' only indicates how safe the transform is once verified.

items.title: Furigana wrappers with truncated readings (visibly wrong on the live site)

items.title: U+FFFD replacement-character mojibake in entry text (kanji/readings/inline-link markers)

items.title: cross_references / prominent_see_also entries without a target_id
items.notes: A dangling reference object lacks target_id. Resolve the intended entry id (build/word_id_lookup.json), or drop the reference if no entry exists. PROGRESS 2026-06-17: detector down 190->136 (180->130 entries). Filled target_id on the 54 refs whose headword AND reading both uniquely match an existing entry (provably-correct exact-match resolution; structural diff confirmed only target_id+modified changed). The remaining 136 are 'headword has no entry' cases that need the drop-or-keep judgment per ref (homophone notes like 00250 工夫/こうふ 'laborer' are deliberately labeled pointers to no-entry words; do NOT bulk-drop). Future runs: verify each, drop only genuine dangling refs, leave intentional homophone/contrast notes. PROGRESS 2026-06-19: detector 136->96. Resolved 40 refs across 37 entries: promoted 22 vestigial `id`->`target_id`, repointed 4 stale ids (01040/02032/00373/00213 -> 02500_shinjin/04555_tenkin/00333_ondo/02869_gaikokujin), added target_id to 14 reading/surface-verified refs (incl. reciprocal kana antonym pairs and kanji variants 堪->耐/満ち潮->満潮/交じる->混じる). Self-checked all 37 via furigana screener: clean (6 flags, all partial-reading/misparse false positives, rejected). REMAINING 96 are mostly INTENTIONAL target-less refs: referenced word has no entry, many are homophone/contrast/antonym display labels that must be KEPT (do NOT drop). Captured 14 entry-worthy referenced words as candidates. Recommend refining the detector to exclude type=homophone/contrast (or labeled) refs whose reading has no entry, so this queue converges instead of flagging permanent intentional pointers. PROGRESS 2026-06-20: detector 96->82. Filled target_id on 13 refs (00296/03477/06242/11797/12070/14705/15551/15688/16184/16466/16476/16900/17729) whose headword AND reading both uniquely match a newly-created 29338-29351 entry (curator restock of antonym/related pairs: 有限/小学/独創/実名/能動/低温/高地/父性/好天/近刊/避寒/大食/答申). Provably-correct exact-match resolution, each target read and semantically confirmed. Self-checked all 13 via furigana screener: clean (2 flags, both false positives — model misread どくそうてき, and 毎年=まいとし is valid — rejected). Captured 4 entry-worthy referenced antonyms as candidates (悪徳/急減/軟質/一神教). REMAINING 82 are overwhelmingly INTENTIONAL target-less pointers (referenced word has no entry; homophone/contrast/antonym display labels that must be KEPT). The detector now mostly flags permanent intentional pointers; refining it to exclude type=homophone/contrast/labeled refs whose reading has no entry would let this queue converge instead of re-surfacing the same ~80 every run. PROGRESS 2026-06-21: RESOLVED. Filled the 5 newly-resolvable refs (06214/12651/12671/13899/16910 -> 29383/29371/29369/29368/29370 curator restock antonym/synonym pairs; each target read and semantically confirmed). 0 resolvable target-less refs now remain dictionary-wide. Implemented the 2026-06-19/06-20 detector recommendation: check_artifacts.py missing-target-id now flags ONLY refs whose referenced word has an entry (resolvable); intentional pointers to no-entry words (homophone/antonym/contrast labels, transitivity-pair pointers) are excluded so the queue converges. `--include-intentional` restores the full 77-item audit list. Self-check (furigana screener) on the 5: 1 flag, a false positive (大切 furigana correct), rejected. Captured 10 entry-worthy referenced words as candidates.

items.title: Concrete semantic tag with no keyword match in the gloss (batch tag drift, P11)
items.notes: P11 is the most pervasive tag-drift problem. The AUTHORITATIVE path for the in-list-but-wrong-category long tail is the accuracy-review mode's LLM tag pass (build/review_accuracy.py --dimensions tags), which judges each semantic tag against the headword (not example topics). For the MECHANICALLY-detectable slices, two high-precision checks were carved out of this noisy heuristic 2026-06-17 and ARE batch_ready: tag-proverb-idiom-mismatch and tag-concrete-noun-domain-mismatch (below). This keyword detector (check_tag_drift.py --check semantic-mismatch) stays batch_ready:false / experimental — it is a free, noisy manual-audit aid only (flags boat=transportation, school=building). Do NOT drive systemic-fix from it; use the two high-precision checks or the accuracy-review tags pass. Remediation prompt: prompts/fix_semantic_tag_drift.md.

items.title: Concrete noun carrying >=2 semantically-distant physical-object domains (P11 garbage multi-tag)
items.filter: optionally add --cohort to restrict to the claude-opus-4-5 batch (highest-density P11 surface)
items.notes: High-precision STRUCTURAL slice of P11: a non-verb headword tagged with two or more mutually-distant hard physical-object domains is the batch garbage multi-tag signature (横断歩道 -> animal-mammal+clothing+transportation; 油絵 -> body-part+tool). Independent of keyword completeness, so it sidesteps the semantic-mismatch noise floor. Measured ~77% clear precision on the first batch (2026-06-17); 18 entries fixed. The residual ~6 are loanword/accessory/fixture polysemy where the dual tag is correct on review (マウス animal+device, 腕時計, ショルダーバッグ, 車席, 電話ボックス, 化粧ポーチ) — VERIFY per entry and KEEP defensible duals; do not force a single tag. Remediation: prompts/fix_semantic_tag_drift.md.

Then it becomes a safe text-substitution systemic-fix validated against the structured tag. Changes visible header text on thousands of pages -> spot-check, curator sign-off on the map.

items.detect: python3 -c "import json,glob; [print(json.load(open(f)).get('id')) for f in glob.glob('entries/*/[0-9]*.json') if json.load(open(f)).get('metadata',{}).get('vocabulary_tier') not in ('basic','core','general')]"
items.notes: A single 2026-06-12 new-entries batch (IDs 29181-29200) shipped with no metadata.vocabulary_tier field at all (absent, not null). schema.json makes the field optional (enum includes null; not in metadata.required) so all 20 validate cleanly and CI never caught them; audit_tiers.py buckets them as unknown, under-counting General by 20. Per CLAUDE.md all new entries are general, and the 20 headwords are ordinary general-tier vocabulary (kenchikushi/datsusara/ensouka/UFO-catcher/etc.), so the correct tier is unambiguous for the whole block. Fix: set vocabulary_tier=general on the 20 IDs, bump modified, rebuild -- no per-entry semantic judgment needed (spot-check the block). Not an ongoing regression: surrounding batches carry the field. Durable follow-up: have validate.py / pre-commit warn on a missing vocabulary_tier (the null-permissive enum lets the omission through silently).

items.title: Inline-link base forms written with furigana braces instead of plain kanji
items.notes: Inline-link syntax is ⟦surface→base：entry_id⟧ where the base slot must be the plain kanji dictionary form. 39 entries instead carry furigana braces in the base slot (⟦{来|き}て→{来|く}る：00254_kuru⟧), pushing wrapper markup into a field that is never rendered as ruby. Measured 2026-07-25 dictionary-wide. Mechanical-safe because the regex is anchored on BOTH sides (→ ... ：) so it cannot escape the base-form slot and cannot touch the surface slot, where braces are correct. Fix: strip { , |reading and } from the base segment only; validate.py; spot-check ~10. Afterwards confirm the resulting base forms resolve in build/word_id_lookup.json -- a braced base form may have been masking a lookup that never worked (see tooling item 11).

items.title: Inline links whose target entry ID does not exist (292 occurrences / 160 entries)
items.detect:
python3 - <<'PY'
import json,re,pathlib
files=sorted(pathlib.Path('entries').rglob('*.json'))
ids={f.stem for f in files}
L=json.load(open('build/word_id_lookup.json',encoding='utf-8'))
LINK=re.compile(r'⟦([^⟧]*?)→([^⟧：]*)：([^⟧]+)⟧')
for f in files:
    for m in LINK.finditer(f.read_text(encoding='utf-8')):
        base,tid=m.group(2).strip(),m.group(3).strip()
        if tid=='noentry' or tid in ids: continue
        cand=L['by_headword'].get(base) or L['by_reading'].get(base) or []
        print(f.stem, base, tid, [c['id'] for c in cand])
PY
items.filter: Work only rows where the candidate list has exactly ONE id (217 of 292) — that is the unambiguous 1:1 repair. Defer rows with 2+ candidates (74: こと/いる/から/後/体 homographs) to per-entry judgment, and the single no-candidate row (逆転する) to candidate creation or a `noentry` conversion.
items.blocked_on: tooling-backlog.md#11 — ship the validate.py target-resolution gate first; the population is iatrogenic (created by inline-link polishing) and will refill if repaired before the gate exists
items.notes: Dictionary-wide scan 2026-07-26: 292 dead links / 144 distinct bad IDs / 160 entries, out of 262,189 inline links (0.11%). Entirely confined to 00000-07999 (the inline-link-polished band), densest at 05000-05999 (112), 03000-03999 (64), 04000-04999 (49). Failure mode is number invention, not word confusion: the romaji in the dead ID is almost always correct and only the digits are wrong (00433_miru -> 00283_miru), which is why no semantic check sees it. Suggested batching: one 1000-ID band per systemic-fix run, worst first; re-run the detect snippet at the end of the run to confirm the band is clear.

items.title: Fabricated conjugation tables from a mis-assigned verb class
items.detect:
python3 -c "import json,glob,re
for f in glob.glob('entries/*/[0-9]*.json'):
    d=json.load(open(f))
    pos=(d.get('metadata',{}).get('tags',{}) or {}).get('pos',[])
    if 'verb-godan' in pos and re.search(r'(える|いる)$', d.get('reading','')): print(d['id'], d['headword'])"
items.notes: A wrong verb-class pos tag makes add_conjugations.py fabricate the ENTIRE conjugation table (06624 甘える tagged verb-godan -> 甘えらない/甘えります/甘えった; 09361 バックレる likewise). Both known cases fixed 2026-07-25 via add_conjugations.py --force. NOT batch_ready: the reading-shape detect command above has a permanent 31-entry false-positive family (入る/返る compounds, 炒る/煎る) and needs an allowlist. The real detector is self-contradiction -- flag a verb entry whose OWN examples contain a conjugated form its declared class cannot produce (甘えた while the table claims 甘えった) -- which has no FP family at all. Build that first (tooling item 35), then this becomes a real, semantically-verified batch. Two cases surfaced from one frontier run's incidental scan, so 2 is a floor, not a total.

items.title: Auxiliary verbs written in kanji in example sentences
items.detect:
python3 -c "import json,glob,re
for f in glob.glob('entries/*/[0-9]*.json'):
    d=json.load(open(f)); s=json.dumps(d,ensure_ascii=False)
    if re.search(r'(?:て|で)\{置\|', s): print(d['id'], d['headword'])"
items.notes: Contemporary Japanese writes AUXILIARY verbs in kana (〜ておく/てみる/ていく/てくる), reserving kanji for the same verbs as MAIN verbs. 01092_oku wrote 〜て{置|お}く in 5 of its own examples while its notes used kana. Measured 2026-07-25 (occurrences/entries): て行く 222/200, て来る 203/34, て見る 168/138, て置く 7/7. NOT batch_ready and NOT mechanical: those counts are a superset -- the same strings are correct when the verb is the MAIN verb of a te-form sequence (持って{来|き}て, 駅で{見|み}た). Only the ておく row (7 entries) is a clean bounded batch. てみる/ていく/てくる need a documented house convention FIRST (example-sentences skill is the natural home) -- a blanket rewrite there is a style imposition, not a correction. Curator decision gates the rest.

items.title: No-pipe brace spans ({コンビニ}, {稀}) — malformed wrappers the furigana detector cannot see
items.notes: Measured 2026-07-27: 887 instances across 616 entries. FURIGANA_PATTERN in build/japanese_utils.py requires a pipe, so these spans are never matched, never stripped, and render as literal curly braces on the live site; all five check_furigana_format.py subpatterns share that assumption, so this family is missing from every P9 scope estimate. Two sub-shapes: (a) kana/loanword spans to de-brace ({コンビニ}, {ゴミ}, {スカート}, {おひたし}); (b) bare kanji with no reading ({稀}, {続}, {匂}, {漸}) which also leave the kanji unglossed. NOT mechanical: a minority are intentional notation that must keep its braces -- {1, 2, 3, ...} set notation (23397 自然数), {X} pattern placeholders, {emotion} category labels. Ship a no-pipe subpattern in check_furigana_format.py with those as a documented reject family (tooling-backlog item 8) before sweeping.

items.title: Mixed bullet markers (・ vs '- ') inside notes fields
items.notes: Measured 2026-07-27: 18,272 line-initial ・ instances across 2,524 entries (~1/12 of the dictionary). Older notes templates use ・ as the list bullet; the house convention is '- '. Both render, and score_note_quality.py's bullet check treats them alike, so nothing surfaces it. Safe rule is doubly anchored: line-initial AND inside the notes field only -- ・ is real punctuation as a compound-name/loanword separator (コーヒー・ブレイク) and as a mid-line list separator, so example sentences, headwords, glosses, and mid-line ・ must not be touched. Sequence: reproduce the count in a detector, sample ~30 entries for line-initial ・ used as genuine punctuation, then sweep in ID blocks with validation after each.

items.title: Adjective examples teaching a phrase where the language uses a set compound (×青い信号 for 青信号)
items.detect: grep the example sentences of the colour/temperature adjective entries for the adjective-plus-noun phrase competing with each enumerated compound (青/赤/黒/白 + 信号/字/板/紙; 熱/冷/温 + 湯/水/蔵; 高/低, 大/小)
items.notes: The adjective phrase is grammatical and faithfully translated, so validate.py, the note scorer and the cross-model accuracy reviewer all pass it -- the defect is idiomaticity, not correctness. Not mechanical: the attributive phrase is often exactly right (青い空), so every hit needs a reader. Bounded because the trigger is a lexicalized N+N compound competing with the adjective's own attributive form, which confines it to enumerable clusters. Scope unmeasured: the first task is the grep, not the sweep.

items.title: Latin characters inside furigana readings ({旅|たbi})
items.detect: scan every {kanji|reading} wrapper for [A-Za-z] inside the reading segment
items.notes: RESOLVED 2026-07-28: all 8 dictionary-wide instances fixed in-run (uncommitted romaji IME input written into the reading verbatim). Kept as a queue entry because the class can refill and the check is free: a Latin letter in a reading is a defect by construction, with no correct case, so any match is a failure and no review queue is needed. Recommended for promotion to a permanent CI check -- see tooling-backlog.md item 24, where the same scan found 7 of the 8 instances the paid furigana screener missed.
